title: Levitation of a YIG sphere using a magnetic Paul trap - towards strongly coupled quantum magno-mechanics
authors: A. O. Yakymenko, S. Das, J. Twamley
abstract: Magnetic levitation offer passive levitation of massive objects for use in advanced inertia sensors, for the generation of non-classical macroscopic motional states, and towards the table-top testing of low energy gravity with quantum mechanics. Magnons, a quanta of spin wave, couple to many physical quantities and strongly to electromagnetic fields, even at room temperature. In this work we demonstrate the stable trapping of a small YIG sphere using a magnetic Paul trap. We present a classical stability analysis of a magnetic Paul trap and show the stability diagram for all mechanical degrees of freedom. We show that coupling between librational and translational modes changes the stability region. We experimentally levitate the soft magnet yttrium iron garnet at room temperature obtaining Q-factors of $\sim25$ and secular frequencies $15.8$ Hz and $17.2$ Hz. We provide numerical estimates of the achievable enhanced coupling between the center-of-mass motion and excited magnon modes, with a cooperativity above unity despite strong mechanical damping, indicating potential applications in quantum information processing, quantum interconnects and quantum memories.
summary: The authors successfully demonstrated the stable levitation of a YIG sphere using a magnetic Paul trap at room temperature. They analyzed the coupled dynamics between the mechanical motion (phonons) and the spin wave excitations (magnons). This work establishes a platform for investigating strongly coupled quantum magno-mechanics, with potential applications in quantum information processing.
main_problem: The work demonstrates stable levitation of a YIG sphere using a magnetic Paul trap, aiming to realize strongly coupled quantum magno-mechanical systems.
main_result: Stable trapping was achieved at room temperature with measured Q-factors ($\sim 25$) and secular frequencies (15.8 Hz, 17.2 Hz), and theoretical estimates suggest achievable magnon-phonon cooperativity above unity.
method: The study combines classical stability analysis using Floquet theory on Mathieu equations with experimental measurements of mechanical motion via backscattered light detection.
model_or_system: The system involves a YIG sphere (soft magnet) trapped by a magnetic Paul trap. The physics couples the center-of-mass mechanical motion (phonons) to the quantized spin waves (magnons), described by coupled Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Q-factors ($\sim 25$), secular frequencies (15.8 Hz, 17.2 Hz), and magnon-phonon cooperativity ($C_{mb}$).
important_parameters: Room temperature operation, magnetic field gradients, and coupling strengths between mechanical and magnonic modes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the classical limit for soft magnets (YIG) and employs small-motion approximations to derive the equations of motion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the stability diagram in parameter space (Fig. 1), the experimental setup using neodymium magnets (Fig. 2), and the measured power spectral density showing trapped oscillations (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the full equations of motion for the coupled system, simplifying them to a vector Mathieu equation for stability analysis, presenting the theoretical framework for magnon-phonon coupling, and concluding with experimental measurements confirming stable levitation and quantifying quantum coupling potential.
why_interesting: This work bridges macroscopic mechanical trapping (Paul traps) with microscopic quantum excitations (magnons), providing an experimentally realized platform to study cavity QED concepts in a solid-state magnetic system, relevant for quantum sensing and information processing.
